## Mo's own task queue, served over MCP. Agents lease a task, check in while
## working, and report it done or failed. A change to anything compiled in,
## meaning this program, job-queue.mo, lib/ or the compiler's output, refuses the
## saved data of a running queue.
module Main
expose JobFilter(..), Page(..), PageError(..), Stats(..), SubmitError(..)
use JobQueue{Queue, Job, QueueError}

max_payload_bytes = 2048
max_jobs = 5000
max_page_jobs = 100
lease_length = 30.minutes
full_advice = "This limit counts every job ever submitted and never falls, so retrying cannot help. Tell a person."

service
  state Queue = JobQueue.empty
  tools submit, lease, heartbeat, acknowledge, fail, list, stats
  every 1.minute expire
  token from env "QUEUE_TOKEN"
end

enum SubmitError
  PayloadTooLarge(limit: Int, bytes: Int)
  QueueFull(limit: Int, advice: Text)
end

enum JobFilter
  AllJobs
  Ready
  Leased
  Done
  Dead
end

enum PageError
  BadPage(after: Int, limit: Int, max_limit: Int)
end

struct Page
  jobs: List(Job)
  next: Option(Int)
  now: Time
end

struct Stats
  total: Int
  ready: Int
  leased: Int
  done: Int
  dead: Int
  limit: Int
  now: Time
end

## Adds a task and returns its id. Every Int in this service, in arguments and
## replies, is a JSON string.
## `payload` is free text handed to a worker unchanged, at most 2,048 bytes. Give
## a short brief and say where the rest is. It is kept for good and any token
## holder can read it, so keep secrets out.
## PayloadTooLarge gives the limit and the size sent: shorten it. HTTP 413 means
## the request body passed 16 KiB, so the payload never reached the queue:
## shorten it.
## QueueFull: the limit of 5,000 counts every job ever submitted, including Done
## and Dead, and never falls. Retrying cannot help, so tell a person.
## Not safe to retry blindly: a retry after a lost reply or store_failed makes a
## second job, so check `list` first.
## Never repeat a call that got handler_failed, work_limit or memory_limit. Five
## of those in 60 seconds restart the service, and three restarts stop it for
## everyone until a person starts it.
fn submit(queue: Queue, _now: Time, payload: Text) : Result((Queue, Int), SubmitError)
  bytes = payload.byte_count
  return Error(PayloadTooLarge(limit: max_payload_bytes, bytes: bytes)) if bytes > max_payload_bytes
  return Error(QueueFull(limit: max_jobs, advice: full_advice)) if JobQueue.jobs(queue).size >=
    max_jobs
  Ok(JobQueue.submit(queue, payload))
end

## {"case":"None"} when nothing is ready, and nothing will notify you. To look
## without taking anything, use `list`. Wait a minute before calling this again.
## {"case":"Some","value":job} gives you the job. A job is {"id","payload",
## "attempts","state"}, and `state` is {"case":"Ready"}, {"case":"Leased","fields":
## {"until":time}}, {"case":"Done"} or {"case":"Dead"}. Pass `job.id` as `id` and
## `job.attempts` as `attempt` to the other tools, and keep both somewhere that
## survives losing your context: no tool tells you which job is yours. The lease ends at
## `job.state.fields.until`. Call `heartbeat` about every 10 minutes.

## Not safe to retry: after a lost reply the job stays held by nobody until the

## A runtime error is {"error":{"kind":"runtime","code":...,"message":...,
## "effect":...}}, where `effect` says what this call did to the queue: none,
## applied or unknown. It does not say whether a retry is safe.

## - handler_failed, work_limit, memory_limit: never repeat the call, and tell a

##   stop it for everyone until a person starts it. With effect none, your lease
##   still ends when it did, so keep working inside it.

##   your id and attempt.

## name the old id in the new payload, because the dead record stays listed.
## Never repeat a call that got handler_failed, work_limit or memory_limit: it
## can stop the service for everyone.
fn list(queue: Queue, now: Time, filter: JobFilter, after: Int, limit: Int) : Result(
  Page,
  PageError

  if after < 0 or limit < 1 or limit > max_page_jobs
    return Error(BadPage(after: after, limit: limit, max_limit: max_page_jobs))

  page = matching.take(limit)
  next = if matching.size > limit: page.last.map(fn(job) job.id end) else: None

## it returns no payloads. Every Int in the reply is a JSON string.
## `total` counts every job ever submitted, including Done and Dead, because jobs
## are never removed. `submit` refuses once `total` reaches `limit`, and that never
## changes, so tell a person when `total` gets close to `limit`.

    ready: ready,
    leased: leased,
    done: done,
    dead: dead,

    now: now
  )

  JobQueue.expire(queue, now)
end

  case filter
    AllJobs: true
    Ready: job.state == JobQueue.Ready
    Leased: job.state is JobQueue.Leased(until: _)
    Done: job.state == JobQueue.Done
    Dead: job.state == JobQueue.Dead
  end

## The core of a job queue. Jobs are submitted, leased to a worker for a while,
## and acknowledged when done. A lease that fails or expires puts its job back
## in the queue, up to three attempts in all; after the third, the job is dead.
## The queue is a value: every operation returns the new queue, and no
## operation ever loses a job.
module JobQueue
expose Queue,
Job(..),
JobState(..),
QueueError(..),
empty,
submit,
lease,
heartbeat,
acknowledge,
fail,
expire,
jobs

max_attempts = 3

struct Job
  id: Int
  payload: Text
  attempts: Int
  state: JobState
end

enum JobState
  Ready
  Leased(until: Time)
  Done
  Dead
end

struct Queue
  jobs: Map(Int, Job)
  next_id: Int
end

enum QueueError
  NoSuchJob(id: Int)
  NotLeased(id: Int)
  BadLease(length: Duration)
end

empty = Queue(jobs: {}, next_id: 1)

fn submit(queue: Queue, payload: Text) : (Queue, Int)
  promise "a submitted job is in the queue, ready"
    result.0.jobs.get(result.1) is Some(job) and job.state == Ready
    allows queue: empty, payload: "x", result: (holding([ready(1)]), 1)
    forbids queue: empty, payload: "x", result: (empty, 1)
  end

  id = queue.next_id
  var after = queue
  after.jobs = after.jobs.set(id, Job(id: id, payload: payload, attempts: 0, state: Ready))
  after.next_id += 1
  (after, id)
end

## Leases the oldest ready job until now + length, counting an attempt. The
## length must be positive, and the lease must end by the year 9999.
fn lease(queue: Queue, now: Time, length: Duration) : Result((Queue, Option(Job)), QueueError)
  promise "a lease never loses a job"
    result is Ok((after, _)) implies queue.jobs.keys.all?(fn(id) after.jobs.has?(id) end)
    allows queue: holding([ready(1)]), now: t0, length: 30.seconds, result: Ok((
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds)]),
      Some(leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds))
    ))
    forbids queue: holding([ready(1)]), now: t0, length: 30.seconds, result: Ok((empty, None))
  end

  examples
    lease(empty, t0, 30.seconds) == Ok((empty, None))
    lease(empty, t0, 0.seconds) == Error(BadLease(length: 0.seconds))
  end

  return Error(BadLease(length: length)) if length <= 0.seconds
  until = try now.checked_add(length).or_fail(BadLease(length: length))
  case queue.jobs.values.find(fn(job) job.state == Ready end)
    None: Ok((queue, None))
    Some(job):
      var taken = job
      taken.state = Leased(until: until)
      taken.attempts += 1
      Ok((put(queue, taken), Some(taken)))
  end
end

## Renews the current lease until now + 30 minutes without counting an attempt.
## NotLeased also covers an expired lease or a different attempt.
fn heartbeat(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result(Queue, QueueError)
  promise "only a current lease can be renewed"
    result is Ok(_) implies
      queue.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and
        job.attempts == attempt and
        job.state is Leased(until: until) and
        until > now
    allows queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.minutes)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 2, result: Ok(
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.minutes)])
    )
  end

  promise "renewing a lease keeps every job and its attempt"
    result is Ok(after) implies queue.jobs.keys.all?(fn(other) after.jobs.has?(other) end)
    result is Ok(after) implies
      after.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and
        job.attempts == attempt and
        job.state is Leased(until: until) and
        now.checked_add(30.minutes) == Some(until)
    allows queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second), ready(2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.minutes), ready(2)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second), ready(2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.minutes)])
    )
  end

  job = try leased_job(queue, now, id, attempt)
  until = try now.checked_add(30.minutes).or_fail(BadLease(length: 30.minutes))
  var renewed = job
  renewed.state = Leased(until: until)
  Ok(put(queue, renewed))
end

## Finishes a current lease. Expired or mismatched attempts return NotLeased.
fn acknowledge(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result(Queue, QueueError)
  promise "only a current lease can be acknowledged"
    result is Ok(_) implies
      queue.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and
        job.attempts == attempt and
        job.state is Leased(until: until) and
        until > now
    allows queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([done(1)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 2, result: Ok(
      holding([done(1)])
    )
  end

  promise "acknowledging finishes the job and keeps every job"
    result is Ok(after) implies queue.jobs.keys.all?(fn(other) after.jobs.has?(other) end)
    result is Ok(after) implies after.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and job.state == Done
    allows queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds), ready(2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([done(1), ready(2)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds), ready(2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([done(1)])
    )
  end

  job = try leased_job(queue, now, id, attempt)
  var finished = job
  finished.state = Done
  Ok(put(queue, finished))
end

## Gives a current lease back after its worker failed: ready again, or dead after
## its last attempt. Expired or mismatched attempts return NotLeased.
fn fail(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result(Queue, QueueError)
  promise "only a current lease can fail"
    result is Ok(_) implies
      queue.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and
        job.attempts == attempt and
        job.state is Leased(until: until) and
        until > now
    allows queue: holding([tried(1, 2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 2, result: Ok(
      holding([retried(1, 2)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([tried(1, 2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([retried(1, 2)])
    )
  end

  promise "a job is attempted at most three times"
    result is Ok(after) and after.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and job.attempts >= max_attempts implies
      job.state == Dead
    allows queue: holding([tried(1, 3)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 3, result: Ok(holding([dead(1)]))
    forbids queue: holding([tried(1, 3)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 3, result: Ok(
      holding([retried(1, 3)])
    )
  end

  examples
    fail(holding([tried(1, 1)]), t0, 1, 1) == Ok(holding([retried(1, 1)]))
    fail(holding([tried(1, 3)]), t0, 1, 3) == Ok(holding([dead(1)]))
    fail(holding([ready(1)]), t0, 1, 0) == Error(NotLeased(id: 1))
    fail(empty, t0, 9, 1) == Error(NoSuchJob(id: 9))
  end

  job = try leased_job(queue, now, id, attempt)
  Ok(release(queue, job))
end

## Gives back every job whose lease ran out by now, as if its worker failed.
fn expire(queue: Queue, now: Time) : Queue
  examples
    expire(holding([leased(1, t0)]), t0) == holding([retried(1, 1)])
    expire(holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second)]), t0) == holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second)])
  end

  var after = queue
  for job in queue.jobs.values
    if job.state is Leased(until: until) and until <= now
      after = release(after, job)
    end
  end
  after
end

## Every job in the queue, in id order, whatever its state.
fn jobs(queue: Queue) : List(Job)
  examples
    jobs(empty) == []
    jobs(holding([ready(1), done(2)])) == [ready(1), done(2)]
    fail(holding([tried(1, 1), ready(2)]), t0, 1, 1).map(jobs) == Ok([retried(1, 1), ready(2)])
  end

  queue.jobs.values
end

fn leased_job(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result(Job, QueueError)
  job = try queue.jobs.get(id).or_fail(NoSuchJob(id: id))
  case job.state
    Leased(until: until): if job.attempts == attempt and until > now: Ok(job) else: Error(
      NotLeased(id: id)
    )
    Ready | Done | Dead: Error(NotLeased(id: id))
  end
end

fn release(queue: Queue, job: Job) : Queue
  var released = job
  released.state = if job.attempts >= max_attempts: Dead else: Ready
  put(queue, released)
end

fn put(queue: Queue, job: Job) : Queue
  var after = queue
  after.jobs = after.jobs.set(job.id, job)
  after
end

t0 = Time.parse("2026-10-12T09:00:00Z") or stop "the time is written correctly"

fn holding(jobs: List(Job)) : Queue
  Queue(jobs: jobs.map(fn(job) (job.id, job) end).to_map, next_id: jobs.size + 1)
end

fn ready(id: Int) : Job
  Job(id: id, payload: "x", attempts: 0, state: Ready)
end

fn leased(id: Int, until: Time) : Job
  Job(id: id, payload: "x", attempts: 1, state: Leased(until: until))
end

fn tried(id: Int, attempts: Int) : Job
  Job(id: id, payload: "x", attempts: attempts, state: Leased(until: t0 + 30.seconds))
end

fn retried(id: Int, attempts: Int) : Job
  Job(id: id, payload: "x", attempts: attempts, state: Ready)
end

fn done(id: Int) : Job
  Job(id: id, payload: "x", attempts: 1, state: Done)
end

fn dead(id: Int) : Job
  Job(id: id, payload: "x", attempts: 3, state: Dead)
end

# Write a finished Mo program

This page is the procedure for a finished Mo program. Correct Mo is Language Reference v0.1. `mo guide --reference` prints that reference. Section 13.4 says this guide covers how to work with the `mo` command, a small complete program with its tests, and when a task is done.

## Know this build

The language headings below use the present tense of the reference.

This build runs `mo check`, `mo run`, `mo test`, `mo format`, `mo fix`, `mo guide`, `mo emit`, `mo serve`, `mo fetch`, `mo push`, `mo replay`, `mo query` and `mo history`. The program below checks with no errors, runs, and passes its examples and its test.

`mo fix FILE` makes each edit that `mo check` shows as an error's only fix, checks again, and prints the errors that are left, as `mo check` does. It rewrites only the files it is given.

`mo emit FILE -o OUT` checks the program as `mo check` does, then writes its bytecode to `OUT`. `-o` is required, and `OUT` is never a source file of the program. A module with neither `main` nor a service is E0079, as for `mo run`, and a file that cannot be written is E1404. This build has no command that runs a bytecode file; run the source with `mo run`.

This build checks, formats, fixes and serves `service ... end` blocks (reference 11.5). `mo test` never reads a service's token, and starts a service on its own only in the service's recovery check, below. Tests and examples can explicitly start one with `Simulation.start(Module, at)`, send registered tools with `Simulation.send(handle, Module.tool, args...)`, advance its fake clock, and crash/restart through the real log and snapshot path backed by an in-memory store. `send` returns the complete declared handler result inside another `Result`; an application `Error` is still inside `Ok`. Helpers may receive the handle. A promise whose inputs include a `Simulation` is E1400; promises over a service's sequences of steps are deferred. `mo run` on a service entry module still refuses with E1408, "mo run does not start services yet". Importing a service module does not start it.

`mo test` runs one recovery check for each service in the program, named after its module, such as `Counter.service.recovery` (reference 12.5). Its author writes nothing for it. It calls tools with generated arguments, advances the fake clock, crashes and restarts the service on an in-memory store, and checks that each restart recovers the state the service held before its crash. `--list` prints it after its module's other checks, and `--only` and `--in` select it. It shares a promise's budget: `--seconds` bounds its time and `--calls` caps its sequences. For `counter.mo` under Run a service, `mo test counter.mo` prints `passed Counter.service.recovery  counter.mo:3:1`, then `1 passed, 0 failed, 0 stopped`. A failing check prints the numbered steps of a shrunk sequence, with literal arguments and each step's outcome, then the state before the crash and the state recovery produced. When the start value stops, the check stops with that bug. When the deadline ends before the check compares a restart, `mo test` reports E1404, "the deadline ended before the check compared a restart".

`mo check --emit=bytecode FILE` prints the program's bytecode as indexed text, with a `services` section holding one descriptor for each module that declares a service, including imported modules. It works on a module without `main`. `mo emit FILE -o OUT` writes the same descriptors and accepts a service without `main`. Neither command evaluates a service's start value or reads its token, and `mo run` still does not start a service (E1408). `mo check --emit=core FILE` shows the start value and timer intervals as ordinary functions but no service registration, so Core output alone cannot reconstruct a service.

A service tool that returns exactly `State` or `Result(State, E)` gets E0101, "a service tool returns only its state". Only `(State, Reply)` and `Result((State, Reply), E)` save new state. `Option(State)`, `List(State)` and records containing state remain read-only replies. A `Result(State, E)` tool receives no fixes. For a bare `State` result, choose between returning `(state, Unit)` to save new state and returning the state inside a record as read-only data. `mo fix` applies neither alternative. The suggested adapters keep the tool's name and `##` comment, move the original function to a helper and rebind the module's references to that helper. Functions on the module's `expose` line receive no fixes because callers in other modules cannot be updated. Functions whose names end in `?` receive no fixes because a `?` name must still return `Bool`. A selected generic handler gets E0100, "a service handler is generic". State, handler inputs and handler results must contain neither capabilities nor function values; E0104 reports this restriction.

Service tool names cannot end in `?` (E0106). Tool arguments after State and Time, projected replies and application errors must have visible fields and cases, including nested types (E0105). Import a wire type with `(..)` to expose its representation. Private service state is not a wire type. E0101 takes precedence over these two checks.

`mo serve` connects a service to MCP clients over authenticated plain HTTP/1.1. HTTP policy, JSON-RPC validation and wire values run in embedded Mo; native code owns sockets, credentials and service dispatch. The transport's byte, node, work and memory ceilings are internal bounds, not language configuration. `mo run` still refuses a service entry module, and Simulation still provides no networking.

Authenticated MCP discovery lists author tools followed by `mo-overview`, `mo-state`, `mo-mailbox`, `mo-timers`, `mo-memory`, `mo-supervisor`, `mo-log`, `mo-export` and `mo-failures`, then the upgrade tools `mo-upgrade-open`, `mo-upgrade-page` and `mo-upgrade-commit`, which change the service and need a second credential, as Upgrade a running service says. The same token grants access to private state. Only the nine operator views are read-only; the three upgrade tools carry `readOnlyHint: false`, and commit carries `destructiveHint: true`. These read-only operator views share the author-call rate limit and do not invoke handlers or enter the mailbox, recovery log or supervisor counts. `mo-state` accepts an optional `path` array of field names and indexes; bounded output marks truncation and `complete: false`, and a value too large to show becomes `{"truncated_bytes": N}` while the values after it still render. A list view that does not fit one reply reports `truncated`, the number of items left out, and `next`, the arguments for the following page: `mo-mailbox` and `mo-timers` take `offset`, `mo-supervisor` takes `after` and `before`, and `mo-log` takes `after`. Separate observations are not one atomic snapshot. `mo-log` retains committed message metadata only since the last snapshot; in-memory supervisor events disappear when the process exits. Live views need the endpoint URL and token, not shell access to the host. `mo-export` with `{"kind":"state"}` starts an immutable MOEX v1 state export; use the returned `next` arguments to read subsequent base64 pages. Each page identifies its export, durable recovery sequence and encoded-state sequence (which can differ after a snapshot failure). The final page releases the pin. A new export replaces the previous state export; 60 seconds without a page expires it. Refused generations never return another export’s bytes. Pins use native memory outside the handler heap. Fetch is available on the service host. `mo-failures` lists retained handler failures and current capture refusals; `after` selects the next record page. A handler failure reports `record: ID` or an explicit `record unavailable` reason before its reply. Application `Error` replies and admission refusals are excluded. Captures preserve pre-call state, arguments, arrival time, budgets, identity and bounded stack context; read-only failures never enter the recovery log. Retention keeps first/latest per kind, up to 64 records and 64 MiB of framed records. A repeating kind replaces its own latest record and never evicts another kind, so a repeat that does not fit is refused. A new kind evicts, as a whole, the kind whose latest record is oldest. Records survive snapshots. `mo-export` accepts `{"kind":"failure","failure":ID}` and has an independent failure pin. On the service host, `mo history`, `mo replay` and `mo query` read a stopped data folder or an artifact without starting the service, as Diagnose a failure offline says.

## The core of a job queue. Jobs are submitted, leased to a worker for a while,
## and acknowledged when done. A lease that fails or expires puts its job back
## in the queue, up to three attempts in all; after the third, the job is dead.
## The queue is a value: every operation returns the new queue, and no
## operation ever loses a job.
module JobQueue
expose Queue,
Job(..),
JobState(..),
QueueError(..),
empty,
submit,
lease,
heartbeat,
acknowledge,
fail,
expire,
jobs

max_attempts = 3

struct Job
  id: Int
  payload: Text
  attempts: Int
  state: JobState
end

enum JobState
  Ready
  Leased(until: Time)
  Done
  Dead
end

struct Queue
  jobs: Map(Int, Job)
  next_id: Int
end

enum QueueError
  NoSuchJob(id: Int)
  NotLeased(id: Int)
  BadLease(length: Duration)
end

empty = Queue(jobs: {}, next_id: 1)

fn submit(queue: Queue, payload: Text) : (Queue, Int)
  promise "a submitted job is in the queue, ready"
    result.0.jobs.get(result.1) is Some(job) and job.state == Ready
    allows queue: empty, payload: "x", result: (holding([ready(1)]), 1)
    forbids queue: empty, payload: "x", result: (empty, 1)
  end

  id = queue.next_id
  var after = queue
  after.jobs = after.jobs.set(id, Job(id: id, payload: payload, attempts: 0, state: Ready))
  after.next_id += 1
  (after, id)
end

## Leases the oldest ready job until now + length, counting an attempt. The
## length must be positive, and the lease must end by the year 9999.
fn lease(queue: Queue, now: Time, length: Duration) : Result((Queue, Option(Job)), QueueError)
  promise "a lease never loses a job"
    result is Ok((after, _)) implies queue.jobs.keys.all?(fn(id) after.jobs.has?(id) end)
    allows queue: holding([ready(1)]), now: t0, length: 30.seconds, result: Ok((
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds)]),
      Some(leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds))
    ))
    forbids queue: holding([ready(1)]), now: t0, length: 30.seconds, result: Ok((empty, None))
  end

  examples
    lease(empty, t0, 30.seconds) == Ok((empty, None))
    lease(empty, t0, 0.seconds) == Error(BadLease(length: 0.seconds))
  end

  return Error(BadLease(length: length)) if length <= 0.seconds
  until = try now.checked_add(length).or_fail(BadLease(length: length))
  case queue.jobs.values.find(fn(job) job.state == Ready end)
    None: Ok((queue, None))
    Some(job):
      var taken = job
      taken.state = Leased(until: until)
      taken.attempts += 1
      Ok((put(queue, taken), Some(taken)))
  end
end

## Renews the current lease until now + 30 minutes without counting an attempt.
## NotLeased also covers an expired lease or a different attempt.
fn heartbeat(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result(Queue, QueueError)
  promise "only a current lease can be renewed"
    result is Ok(_) implies
      queue.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and
        job.attempts == attempt and
        job.state is Leased(until: until) and
        until > now
    allows queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.minutes)])

    forbids queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 2, result: Ok(
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.minutes)])
    )
  end

  promise "renewing a lease keeps every job and its attempt"
    result is Ok(after) implies queue.jobs.keys.all?(fn(other) after.jobs.has?(other) end)
    result is Ok(after) implies
      after.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and
        job.attempts == attempt and
        job.state is Leased(until: until) and
        now.checked_add(30.minutes) == Some(until)

    forbids queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second), ready(2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.minutes)])

  end

  job = try leased_job(queue, now, id, attempt)
  until = try now.checked_add(30.minutes).or_fail(BadLease(length: 30.minutes))

## Finishes a current lease. Expired or mismatched attempts return NotLeased.
fn acknowledge(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result(Queue, QueueError)
  promise "only a current lease can be acknowledged"
    result is Ok(_) implies
      queue.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and
        job.attempts == attempt and
        job.state is Leased(until: until) and
        until > now
    allows queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([done(1)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 2, result: Ok(
      holding([done(1)])
    )
  end

  promise "acknowledging finishes the job and keeps every job"
    result is Ok(after) implies queue.jobs.keys.all?(fn(other) after.jobs.has?(other) end)
    result is Ok(after) implies after.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and job.state == Done
    allows queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds), ready(2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([done(1), ready(2)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([leased(1, t0 + 30.seconds), ready(2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([done(1)])
    )
  end

  job = try leased_job(queue, now, id, attempt)
  var finished = job
  finished.state = Done
  Ok(put(queue, finished))
end

## Gives a current lease back after its worker failed: ready again, or dead after
## its last attempt. Expired or mismatched attempts return NotLeased.
fn fail(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result(Queue, QueueError)
  promise "only a current lease can fail"
    result is Ok(_) implies
      queue.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and
        job.attempts == attempt and
        job.state is Leased(until: until) and
        until > now
    allows queue: holding([tried(1, 2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 2, result: Ok(
      holding([retried(1, 2)])
    )
    forbids queue: holding([tried(1, 2)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 1, result: Ok(
      holding([retried(1, 2)])
    )
  end

  promise "a job is attempted at most three times"
    result is Ok(after) and after.jobs.get(id) is Some(job) and job.attempts >= max_attempts implies
      job.state == Dead
    allows queue: holding([tried(1, 3)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 3, result: Ok(holding([dead(1)]))
    forbids queue: holding([tried(1, 3)]), now: t0, id: 1, attempt: 3, result: Ok(
      holding([retried(1, 3)])
    )
  end

  examples
    fail(holding([tried(1, 1)]), t0, 1, 1) == Ok(holding([retried(1, 1)]))
    fail(holding([tried(1, 3)]), t0, 1, 3) == Ok(holding([dead(1)]))
    fail(holding([ready(1)]), t0, 1, 0) == Error(NotLeased(id: 1))
    fail(empty, t0, 9, 1) == Error(NoSuchJob(id: 9))
  end

  job = try leased_job(queue, now, id, attempt)
  Ok(release(queue, job))
end

## Gives back every job whose lease ran out by now, as if its worker failed.
fn expire(queue: Queue, now: Time) : Queue
  examples
    expire(holding([leased(1, t0)]), t0) == holding([retried(1, 1)])
    expire(holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second)]), t0) == holding([leased(1, t0 + 1.second)])
  end

  var after = queue
  for job in queue.jobs.values
    if job.state is Leased(until: until) and until <= now
      after = release(after, job)
    end
  end
  after
end

## Every job in the queue, in id order, whatever its state.
fn jobs(queue: Queue) : List(Job)
  examples
    jobs(empty) == []
    jobs(holding([ready(1), done(2)])) == [ready(1), done(2)]
    fail(holding([tried(1, 1), ready(2)]), t0, 1, 1).map(jobs) == Ok([retried(1, 1), ready(2)])
  end

  queue.jobs.values
end

fn leased_job(queue: Queue, now: Time, id: Int, attempt: Int) : Result(Job, QueueError)
  job = try queue.jobs.get(id).or_fail(NoSuchJob(id: id))
  case job.state
    Leased(until: until): if job.attempts == attempt and until > now: Ok(job) else: Error(
      NotLeased(id: id)
    )
    Ready | Done | Dead: Error(NotLeased(id: id))
  end
end

fn release(queue: Queue, job: Job) : Queue
  var released = job
  released.state = if job.attempts >= max_attempts: Dead else: Ready
  put(queue, released)
end

fn put(queue: Queue, job: Job) : Queue
  var after = queue
  after.jobs = after.jobs.set(job.id, job)
  after
end

`mo serve` exits with one of these statuses:

- 0: SIGTERM or SIGINT stopped it. It closes its port, so a new connection is refused, and finishes the open ones first, which their deadlines bound to about 25 seconds.
- 1: the program has errors, or it could not start (E1409).
- 2: a mistake in the command.
- 69: supervision (D308) stopped the service. Five failures within a minute restart it, and three restarts within ten minutes stop it. It stays down until a person starts it, as Recover from a stop says.
- 70: it died any other way, such as a failed save, a listener failure or a bug in a module constant. Starting it again is safe.
- 75: another process held the store for the whole wait. Nothing was changed, and starting it again is safe, so a service manager should retry it.

Initialize returns an `MCP-Session-Id`. A client that sends it on `GET /mcp` with `Accept: text/event-stream` receives `notifications/tools/list_changed` after each activation; each session has one stream, and a new GET replaces it. Notifications are not a durable log: a reconnecting client calls `tools/list`. POST calls work with or without the session header.

If a checked restart is refused and the program cannot be repaired within those checks, use the fresh-folder fallback. Start the old program on the old `DIR`, read what you need through its tools, and stop it. Start the fixed program on a new, empty `DIR` and send that data to its tools. revision,
Job(..),

QueueError(..),
empty,

heartbeat,
acknowledge,
fail,
